name: 035.2 — geometry: pad, and the insets that move content
author: brodgar
description: Self-checking suite for task 035.2: the stylesheet learns to MOVE things. `pad` joins font/color/bg/border as a style property, and it — together with a border's own 9-slice insets — feeds iresize/contarea, the one place that decides where a window's content starts. This is the task where the automation pays: every claim is a number the rule predicts in advance. Asserts: the refusals (a pad that is not a number — LuaJ says a numeric STRING is a number, so this is type-checked, not isnumber()-checked; a negative pad; an unknown property, whose message now names pad); that widget:style() and widget:skin() both report pad; that a pad-only rule is enough to dress a window and grows its OUTER size by exactly twice the pad while the CONTENT does not move (the ctor's size is the content size and the deco frames it — the direction that silently shrinks every window if reversed); that changing a pad re-lays the window out without rebuilding its chrome; that with a border the window's size is content + insets + 2*pad EXACTLY and content starts one pad inside those insets; that dropping either rule restores the previous numbers exactly, not approximately; that a window.frame SITE rule pads every window the same way; and that a pad on a surface owning no geometry (a text site key, a widget with no chrome) is inert rather than an error. One [manual] line for what a program cannot judge — whether content visibly sits where the padding says; ':t035-2 look' parks the framed theme on. Its probes are destroyed and its sheet dropped, so a login that runs it leaves the client stock.
